beliefs: Every character is shifted by ASCII +1 (a→b, A→B, 0→1, space→!, ~→DEL) [E1, E5, E7]
After shifting, the FIRST character of each maximal run of lowercase letters is uppercased; subsequent lowercase letters keep their raw +1 shift [E12, E13, E14, E16]
Uppercase letters, digits, spaces, and symbols get only the raw +1 shift with no case change (A→B, Z→[, 0→1) [E1, E2, E7, E11, E17]
Runs of lowercase are broken by any non-lowercase character, so 'aB'→'Bc' and 'Ba'→'Cb' [E12, E13, E14, E16, E17]
When the first char of a lowercase run is 'z', its shifted result '{' is uppercased to '[' [E8, E11, E15]
The uppercase step applies only to the first char of a lowercase run, so 'ab'→'Bc', 'aa'→'Bb', 'baa'→'Cbb' [E12, E13, E14]
The 'z'→'[' uppercase exception applies to every run-start 'z', including 'zz'→'[{', 'zzz'→'[{{', 'zzaz'→'[{b{' [E15]
Uppercase letters are NOT lowercased after shifting; they stay as their +1 shifted uppercase/symbol (A→B, Z→[) [E7, E11, E16, E17]
notes: E17 confirms v16's run-breaking rule was already right for lowercase runs; the only error was that uppercase letters were being uppercased again by the shift. The fix: only uppercase the shifted result when the original char is lowercase (and is a run-start). Uppercase originals get a plain +1 shift with no case change.
